profile.reading:
Segra's Charlotte data center campus is made up of two purpose built colocation buildings, Charlotte One and Charlotte Two, standing across the street from each other on International Airport Drive near Charlotte Douglas International Airport. Segra is a fiber network and data center operator headquartered in Charlotte, North Carolina, and the company's own facility sheets, published on its website, describe both buildings in detail.

Charlotte One, at 3100 International Airport Drive, is the smaller of the two buildings: roughly 7,800 square feet in total with about 5,000 square feet of raised data center floor, backed by 500 kilowatts of power capacity under what Segra calls a 100 percent power service level agreement. Charlotte Two, next door at 3101 International Airport Drive, is substantially larger, about 28,000 square feet overall with roughly 14,032 square feet of data floor and 2.5 megawatts of power capacity, also carrying a 100 percent power SLA.

Both buildings share a common design approach: N+1 redundant cooling in a hot aisle and cold aisle configuration, redundant UPS systems, N+1 backup generators, layered physical security with continuous video surveillance and biometric access control, and 24x7x365 staffed network operations. Both are SSAE 16 SOC 2 Type II certified and PCI DSS and HIPAA compliant, and both are marketed as carrier neutral with diverse fiber entry points, a 100 Gbps network backbone, and multi cloud connectivity to AWS and Azure. Charlotte Two additionally lists a dry pipe pre-action fire suppression system with 129 active smoke detectors, reflecting its larger footprint.

Segra operates this Charlotte campus alongside other North Carolina facilities in Kannapolis, Raleigh, and Winston-Salem, and describes its combined colocation portfolio as spanning seven data center facilities. As a fiber and network services company rather than a hyperscale or wholesale colocation provider, Segra's data centers are generally smaller footprint, enterprise oriented facilities designed around network diversity and compliance certifications rather than the scale metrics associated with hyperscale campuses. The company's own published materials do not give a construction or opening year for either Charlotte building, nor do they identify specific tenants, so those details remain undocumented in what the operator has chosen to publish.

[batch narration moved out of reading 2026-09-02] Segra is a fiber and data center services provider based in Charlotte, North Carolina. This specific facility level reading supplements an earlier operator level pass already on file for this operator, which found a corporate headquarters address, 11215 North Community House Road, explicitly not confirmed as tied to any specific data center facility. This operators own current site names two distinct Charlotte facilities, Charlotte One Data Center and Charlotte Two Data Center, separate from a third Kannapolis facility and the corporate headquarters. A facility specific aggregator listing independently corroborates this naming, giving Segra Charlotte 1 at 3100 International Airport Drive and Segra Charlotte 2 at 3101 International Airport Drive, both Charlotte 28208, essentially across the street from each other. Since this registry carries only one generic Charlotte row for this operator and this session could not confirm which of the two named buildings it represents, both addresses are applied together as the shared campus location rather than attributing the row to only one building. The separate Kannapolis facility is not represented by this row and is not applied here.

reading.body:
SEGRA in Charlotte publishes no power capacity, compute density, or cooling specifications for this facility. The campus consists of two adjacent buildings at International Airport Drive, both named by the operator as separate Charlotte colocation data centers, but without published IT load or infrastructure detail this reading cannot assess their significance to AI scaling.

North Carolina has 19 mapped data center facilities and only 5 with published power capacity totaling 50 MW. This campus would rank sixth by published capacity if it had disclosed a figure, but since it has not, its position in the state's infrastructure cannot be determined.

Without specifications, this campus cannot be read as material to decisions about AI grid constraints in its region or beyond.
